clue.text: Stargazer's firm and hurtful, dismissing moon

definitions.note: the stargazer is, with 's standing for 'is'

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so the moon's letters are removed from the longer word

parts.note: pernicious means harmful or hurtful
Io is one of Jupiter's moons

explanation.surface: An astronomer is said to be stern and unkind, with the moon left out of the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Stargazer' is read as 'is', linking definition to wordplay; 'moon' is not our Moon but one of Jupiter's.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicolaus Copernicus was the Renaissance astronomer who put the Sun at the centre of the solar system.

clue.text: Celeb spotted revolutionary nicking rare film

parts.note: a celebrity is a star

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
revolutionary means turning round, so the word for spotted is read backwards

parts.note: spotted means saw
R is an abbreviation for rare, as on a steak order

explanation.surface: A famous person is seen with a radical who steals an uncommon movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a rebel describing a person, but it only turns the word for spotted round before it takes in R.
explanation.definitionFit: Star Wars is George Lucas's 1977 space-opera movie and the franchise that followed it.

clue.text: Top nut occupies spot on height

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the first part sits on top of the letter for height
occupies means takes up the space within, so the printer's measure sits inside the pimple

parts.note: a zit is a spot on the skin
an en, or nut, is a printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: A pimple sits on someone's head at the top of a tall figure.
explanation.walkthrough: In printing an en is also called a nut, a typesetter's term for that width of space.
explanation.definitionFit: The zenith is the highest point or peak of something, so it means the top.

clue.text: Priest embraces perfect couple

indicators.note: embraces means hugs, so the priest's letters go round the letters for perfect

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or perfect, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A clergyman hugs a flawless married couple.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, first-class, is often written AI in crosswords, the figure one doubling as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is two of a kind together, the same as a couple.

clue.text: Enthused, a couple of students sack party

parts.note: L stands for learner or student, as on a learner driver's plate, so two of them are LL
to sack someone is to fire them
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Two students get excited and kick out a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is a Northern Irish political party, the Democratic Unionist Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all fired up means feeling eager and excited, the same state as enthused.

clue.text: Music firm once blocking old unaccompanied Elvis hit

indicators.note: blocking means standing in the way, so the record company sits inside the word for unaccompanied

parts.note: solo means alone, unaccompanied
EMI was a British record company

explanation.surface: A record label once stood in the way of an old solo Elvis single.
explanation.walkthrough: Elvis's It's Now or Never set new words to the tune of the Neapolitan song O Sole Mio, so the setter is stretching a point.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neapolitan song's melody became Elvis Presley's chart-topping single, so it counts loosely as his hit.

clue.text: Brilliant cryptic clue books

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the letters of clue are scrambled

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A solver praises a crossword clue as brilliant, found in some books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brilliant cryptic clue' reads like praise for the puzzle, but 'cryptic' is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucent means shining or glowing with light, so brilliant in the sense of bright.

clue.text: 'Let It Be' record released by music group

definitions.note: a proofreader's instruction meaning leave the text as it was

indicators.note: released by means let go by, so the record's letters leave the group's name

parts.note: a septet is a group of seven musicians
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: The Beatles' Let It Be is a record put out by a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let It Be' looks like the Beatles song, but it is the plain meaning of the Latin proofreading mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is Latin for 'let it stand', written by an editor to cancel a correction.

clue.text: Performing with the bishop, everyone's alert

parts.note: a performer on stage is on
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
everyone means all

explanation.surface: A cleric joins a show, and everybody is wide awake.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of everyone's is read as 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the ball is an idiom for being quick-witted and attentive, which is being alert.

clue.text: Slow growth of fruits over on top of tree

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for fruits is read backwards

parts.note: nuts are a kind of fruit

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, here of tree

explanation.surface: Fruit develops slowly because of something wrong with the top of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: To stunt the growth of something is to check it, so the definition takes 'of' along.
explanation.definitionFit: To stunt something is to hold back its development, so it means to slow its growth.

clue.text: Peer at one monarch once

parts.note: an earl is a peer of the realm
I is the Roman numeral for one
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A lord stares at one former king or queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer at' looks like a verb, staring; it is a noun, a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier means at a previous time, and once is a way of saying formerly.

clue.text: Short drunk guy's gleaming

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the last letter is dropped from the word for drunk

parts.note: full is slang for drunk
a gent is a man, a guy

explanation.surface: A small inebriated man is glowing.
explanation.walkthrough: Full is British slang for drunk; FULL short is FUL. The 's of guy's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fulgent is a literary word for shining brightly, the same as gleaming.

clue.text: New planet lacking core at a lower level formerly

indicators.note: lacking core means missing the central letter, which is taken from the planet

parts.note: Earth is a planet

explanation.surface: A newly found world without a centre lies lower down, in older times.
explanation.walkthrough: The core of a five-letter word is its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Neath is an old poetic shortening of beneath, meaning underneath or below.

clue.text: Subject quietly matures after treatment with heroin

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: after treatment means once processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Someone grows up calmly after being treated with a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled letters are those of matures plus H, giving UREMATHS after P.
explanation.definitionFit: Pure maths is an academic discipline of abstract mathematics, a school or university subject.

clue.text: Where to see stars arrange film song

parts.note: to plan is to arrange
ET is Spielberg's film about an extraterrestrial
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: Organising a movie and music is how to meet celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' suggests film stars, beside the film and song, but these are the night sky's.
explanation.definitionFit: Planetaria are domed theatres projecting images of the night sky and its heavenly bodies.

clue.text: Lord's big shot edgy about Home Secretary's telepathy?

parts.note: Lord's is the London cricket ground, and a six is the biggest hit in cricket

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for edgy goes round the Home Secretary's letters

parts.note: edgy means tense
HS is an abbreviation for Home Secretary

explanation.surface: A peer's important man is nervous around a senior British minister who reads minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lord's' looks like a nobleman; Lord's is the cricket ground in London, where a six clears the boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: A sixth sense is a supposed intuitive faculty beyond the five senses; telepathy is one example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Cox tours Lapland excitedly indicating stars

indicators.note: excitedly means in an agitated way, so the letters of the three words are shuffled

explanation.surface: Professor Brian Cox tours Lapland in excitement, pointing out the stars.
explanation.walkthrough: Brian Cox is a British physicist and TV presenter of astronomy programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Castor and Pollux are the two brightest stars in the constellation Gemini, the heavenly twins.

clue.text: In Paris they talk about Oscar being conditionally freed

indicators.note: about means around, so the French phrase goes round the letter for Oscar

parts.note: on parle is French for 'they talk' or 'one speaks'
Oscar is the NATO alphabet word for O

explanation.surface: Parisians gossip about an Oscar winner released under conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner on parole has been released early on condition of good behaviour.

clue.text: Foreign articles on singing star rocket

parts.note: la and un are the French words for 'the' and 'a', articles in a foreign language
Cher is an American pop singer

explanation.surface: Overseas newspaper pieces report on a famous vocalist's rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A launcher is a device that fires a missile, and a rocket can be one, as in a rocket launcher system.

clue.text: C&A perhaps distributed crates here?

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the letters of the first two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: The clothing chain C&A might have handed out boxes here.
explanation.walkthrough: C&A is a European clothing retailer that left Britain in 2001; 'crates' are also slang for old cars, which end up on the dump.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapheap is a pile of junk where worn-out old cars, called crates in slang, are dumped.

clue.text: Nice guy, say, stands up to go back

parts.note: René is a French man's name, and Nice is a French city

indicators.note: stands up means rises, which in a down clue reads the letters bottom to top

parts.note: e.g. means for example, 'say'

explanation.surface: A pleasant man rises to his feet to make a return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the adjective; it is the French city, making the guy a Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: To renege is to go back on a promise or deal, failing to honour it.

clue.text: Keep quiet about unfashionable quarter

indicators.note: about means around, so the hush goes round the word for unfashionable

parts.note: sh is the instruction to keep quiet
out means out of fashion

explanation.surface: Someone stays silent about a dowdy district of town.
explanation.definitionFit: South is one of the four cardinal points, each called a quarter of the compass.

clue.text: Second woman's cutting training field

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the woman's word goes into the letters for training

parts.note: PE is physical education, training in sport
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A second woman is mowing the training pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field' suggests a sports ground, given training, but means an area of activity.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere is a domain of interest or activity, as is a field of study.

clue.text: After excavation, oddly reveal Athena's alter ego

indicators.note: after means following, so the odd letters come behind the excavation

parts.note: a mine is an excavation in the ground

indicators.note: oddly means taking the odd-placed letters, first, third and fifth, of reveal

explanation.surface: Digging up the ground shows something strange about the Greek goddess's other self.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman goddess of wisdom matches the Greek Athena, her counterpart under another name.

clue.text: Writing about Arab world

indicators.note: about means around, so the manuscript's letters go round the abbreviation for Arab

parts.note: MS is manuscript, a piece of writing
AR is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: Something written about the Arab world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab world' runs together in the surface, but 'world' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars is a planet, and planets are often called worlds.

clue.text: Clive set out to patrol fringes of English Channel

indicators.note: to patrol means going round, so the rearranged name surrounds the edges
set out means arranged, so the letters of Clive are rearranged
fringes of means the outer letters, first and last, of English

explanation.surface: A man called Clive sets off to keep watch over the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English Channel' runs together in the surface; 'Channel' alone is the definition. VICLE from Clive goes around EH.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle is a medium for conveying something, as a channel is, like a vehicle for ideas.

clue.text: Test quartet in Virginia

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the four sits within the state's letters

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia
IV is the Roman numeral four

explanation.surface: A four-piece band takes an exam in Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: A viva, short for viva voce, is the oral exam a British doctoral student must pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A viva is an oral examination, a spoken test at university.

clue.text: Stage Irish revolts star

indicators.note: revolts means turns over, so both pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: Stage Irish characters rise up against a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage Irish' reads as a caricature phrase, but stage is a leg and Irish is IR.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigel is the brightest star in the constellation Orion.

clue.text: Northern city, where to find Nemo vessel

parts.note: Captain Nemo appears in the novels of Jules Verne, so he is found in Verne
SS is steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: A northern city is where Nemo's submarine can be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nemo vessel' suggests the Nautilus, but Nemo is found in VERNE and the vessel is SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverness is the main city of the Scottish Highlands, in the far north of Britain.
